Title: Patrologiae graecae tomus CLII: Manuel Calecas, Joan. Cyparissiota, Matth. Cantacuzenus, alii. Manuelis Calecae ordinis Fratrum Praedicatorum, Constantinopolitani patriarchae(?), Opera omnia. Accedunt Joannis Cyparissiotae, Matthaei Cantacuzeni scripta theologica et exegetica; necnon Joannis Glycis, Esaiae, Joannis Calecae, Isidori, Callisti, Philothei CPolitanorum patriarcharum diplomata, synodicae constitutiones, epistolae
Creator: Manuel Calecas, of the Order of Preachers; John Cyparissiotes; Matthew Kantakouzenos; and the patriarchs of Constantinople John Glykys, Esaias, John Calecas, Isidore, Callistus and Philotheos (documents 1310-1372); Greek texts with parallel Latin, edited by J.-P. Migne
Publisher: Paris: J.-P. Migne (Petit-Montrouge), Patrologiae cursus completus, Series graeca, tomus 152
Publication Date: 1866
Rights: Public Domain
Rights basis: the title page reads '1866' in this scan's OCR (file line 201); the list of Migne's volumes in tomus CLXI (file line 110907 of the Bessarion volume) reads 'CLII (1865)'; either year is far before 1930. Host record: date field 1857, possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT.
Language: grc (Greek with parallel or following Latin translation; the Latin and Greek share the OCR file; see the content note)
Source: Internet Archive item patrologicursus63migngoog (archive.org/details/patrologicursus63migngoog), full-text file patrologicursus63migngoog_djvu.txt, fetched directly by the Library thread, October 2026.
Provenance note: Header prepended by the Library thread; the OCR text follows it unchanged. Nothing was stripped, normalised, corrected, re-spaced or retyped (the long s glyph occurs 0 times and was left as found). The Google Books boilerplate page at the head of the OCR is left in place. The OCR text that follows is 5377926 bytes, 3981657 characters and 109888 lines. OCR quality sampled at the title pages and at about 5%, 50% and 95% of the file (lines 5507, 54957 and 104406): Latin clean; Greek polytonic readable with chi for kappa slips; patriarchal documents readable (line 101109).
Content note: Tomus 152 as its ELENCHUS lists it: Manuel Calecas, Against the errors of the Greeks (four books, Latin from the Greek by Ambrose of Camaldoli), De essentia et operatione, De fide; John Cyparissiotes, the 'Palamitic Transgressions' book one and the Exposition in ten decades (an anti-Palamite voice); Matthew Kantakouzenos's commentaries on the Song of Songs and Wisdom; and, from col. 1033, the patriarchal diplomata, synodal constitutions and letters of John Glykys, Esaias, John Calecas, Isidore, Callistus and Philotheos from 1310 to 1372. Calecas the writer (d. 1410) is a different man from the patriarch John Calecas (deposed 1347).
